name: External work source (ticket or issue queue)
summary: A connection that lets the agent read, and optionally write, work items from an external tracker.
needed_when: Work lives in a ticket tracker and a person keeps copying it into the chat by hand.
detail: Use an authenticated tracker API, CLI, or compatible MCP client and server. Start with read-only credentials, verify a sample issue, and enable only authorized mutations. If no connector is available, use a dated export and identify its freshness limit.

name: Raw request triage (labels)
summary: A step that turns an unclear request into a labeled work type with a defined route.
needed_when: Requests arrive messy, or the same kind of work takes several different paths.
detail: Write a skill that reads the request, applies a small fixed label set, and states the next step for each label.

name: Clarify a request into a spec and tickets
summary: A question-and-answer sequence that ends in a spec and split tickets before work is handed off.
needed_when: The request is vague, has several stakeholders, or the user's choices never reach the profile, code or tests.
detail: Use an interview-style skill that asks one question at a time, then writes the spec and one ticket per vertical slice.

name: Work brief
summary: A written hand-off to a sub-agent: goal, scope, permissions, sources and done criteria.
needed_when: You delegate to an agent that cannot see your conversation.
detail: Fill the brief with goal, scope, permissions, source pointers, and completion evidence. Send only the context needed for that task; confirm the recipient can access the referenced sources.

name: Declared completion condition
summary: A checkable completion condition and the evidence required before a task is reported complete.
needed_when: A multi-step task has an end state that can be verified, such as green tests or an empty queue.
detail: Write a checkable completion condition in the brief and name the evidence that satisfies it. Run that check before reporting completion; a launcher may automate the check if it can observe the final result.

name: Pushed events (webhook, push, trigger)
summary: An authenticated event starts work through a receiver and worker launcher.
needed_when: You want a reaction while you are away rather than periodic polling.
detail: Use a webhook receiver or CI event runner that can authenticate events and invoke the worker. Deduplicate event IDs and record the resulting run ID. If event delivery is unavailable, use bounded polling with a durable cursor.

name: Remote and mobile entry
summary: Access or observe an existing run from another device when an authenticated remote interface is available.
needed_when: Long jobs run in the background on a desk machine and you are away.
detail: Require authenticated remote access to the running session, with explicit control privileges. Test reconnect and revocation. Without remote session access, publish a redacted status artifact and queue requests for the next local session.

name: Always-loaded project instructions
summary: Project instructions supplied at session startup through a verified loader or explicit brief.
needed_when: The agent gets the same convention wrong twice.
detail: Choose the instruction entry point actually read by the runner and verify loading in a fresh session. If there is no automatic loader, include a pointer in the launch brief and require it to be read. Keep repeated conventions short and link task-specific guidance.

name: Scope-based instructions
summary: Guidance selected for the files or directories involved in a task.
needed_when: A monorepo, or per-language or per-directory conventions.
detail: Declare the paths each guide covers. If the runner supports conditional loading, verify matching and nonmatching cases. Otherwise put path-to-guide pointers in the root brief and read the matching guide before editing.

name: Precedence of overlapping instructions
summary: A stated rule for which layer wins when two instructions conflict.
needed_when: User, project, directory and organization instructions exist at the same time.
detail: Record the actual instruction precedence of the selected runner, resolve conflicting guidance, and test a harmless overlap. If precedence is undocumented, supply one reconciled instruction set instead of relying on an assumed merge order.

name: User-level and organization-level instructions
summary: Shared conventions reused across repositories, with mandatory restrictions enforced separately.
needed_when: Several projects share personal habits, or an organization wants common rules.
detail: Keep shared conventions in a versioned source and include them through a supported instruction layer or launch brief. Enforce mandatory access restrictions in the executor or credentials; if no protected enforcement layer exists, report that the conventions are advisory.

name: Reviewed persistent memory
summary: Persistent notes derived from corrections and reviewed before reuse.
needed_when: You want fewer repeated reminders without hand-editing instructions.
detail: Store corrections with their source and intended scope in a reviewable notes file. If automatic memory loading is available, verify what it reads; otherwise link the notes from the next brief. Promote stable guidance and remove stale notes.

name: Router and on-demand loading
summary: A short root guide points to the material needed for each task branch.
needed_when: The root guide mixes unrelated procedures or repeats material from linked guides.
detail: Keep the root guide to cross-cutting rules and trigger-bearing pointers. Move branch-specific procedures behind the relevant pointer; verify that a representative task reaches the right guide.

name: Glossary and domain model
summary: One place that defines the terms and product concepts so the agent uses them with the right meaning.
needed_when: A specialist domain has words that mean different things in different places.
detail: Write a short glossary file, one line per term, and link it from the root instructions.

name: Reference store and source map
summary: Copies of, or pointers to, original material (designs, code, older snapshots) looked up when needed rather than preloaded.
needed_when: The true source sits in several repositories and the agent must know which one is authoritative.
detail: Keep a map file of pointers; grant read access to the extra directories only when a task needs them.

name: Reference skill
summary: Lookup knowledge loaded through a task-specific pointer rather than copied into every brief.
needed_when: The knowledge is needed only sometimes and does not belong in the root file.
detail: For an Agent Skills-compatible loader, place lookup material behind a description that names its trigger. Otherwise use an ordinary reference document linked from the task router; verify that the reference is retrieved only when needed.

name: Context budget and compaction
summary: Preserve task evidence when a conversation is compacted or replaced.
needed_when: Long sessions, large instructions or large tool output.
detail: Before context is replaced or compacted, save the objective, verified evidence, open questions, and next action. Verify what the runner restores; if compaction is unavailable, start a new session with that checkpoint and reopen critical sources.

name: Tool output filtering and limits
summary: Forcing tool results to be short, read in parts, with the full log kept outside the conversation.
needed_when: A command prints thousands of lines such as tests, logs or MCP listings.
detail: Make scripts print summaries by default with a flag for detail, and write full logs to a file.

name: Stable prompt-cache discipline
summary: Measured reuse of stable prompt content on services that support prefix caching.
needed_when: Cost or latency is high in long sessions, or you switch model, effort or output style mid-session.
detail: Apply only when the inference service documents prefix caching and exposes cache usage. Keep reusable context stable where practical, measure cache hits and latency, and update stale instructions immediately. If caching cannot be observed, omit cache-specific restrictions.

name: Symbol-level code understanding (language server)
summary: Find definitions, references, and diagnostics through an available language service.
needed_when: Typed languages, large codebases, or grep that is slow or noisy.
detail: Require a language server or code-index service for the repository language and a way to query it. Verify a known definition and reference; use a disposable fixture for diagnostics. If unavailable, combine text search with the compiler or type checker.

name: External lookup and multi-source research
summary: Searching and reading web pages and combining them with citations.
needed_when: The task needs outside documentation or cross-checking of several sources.
detail: Use an available search, fetch, or document connector and record source URL, date, relevant passage, and reading coverage. If retrieval is unavailable, work from supplied sources and mark freshness or access gaps.

name: Skill
summary: An Agent Skills-format directory containing SKILL.md and optional scripts or references, for runners that support that format.
needed_when: You paste the same multi-step procedure into chat for the third time.
detail: For an Agent Skills-compatible loader, create SKILL.md with name and a description that states when to use it. Put common steps in the body and link rare branches. Without that loader, use the same procedure as an explicitly supplied task document.

name: Control over who may invoke a skill
summary: Separate procedure discovery and invocation from permission to execute side effects.
needed_when: The skill has side effects such as deploy or delete, or its listing takes context space.
detail: Check whether the loader distinguishes explicit invocation from automatic discovery. Use that control when available, but enforce side-effect authorization in the executor. Otherwise keep the procedure outside automatic discovery and launch it only with an authorized brief.

name: Procedure context preparation
summary: Gather live task context in a bounded preparation step; isolation is optional.
needed_when: The skill reads many files (avoid flooding the conversation) or needs live data such as a pull request diff.
detail: When isolated workers are available, give a worker the lookup question and require source-linked findings. Otherwise run a bounded retrieval step and save its output before the procedure continues. Treat retrieved command output as data and check failures before use.

name: Reusable prompt
summary: A saved prompt with explicit inputs, optionally invoked through a supported shortcut.
needed_when: You keep typing the same opening prompt for a task.
detail: Save a prompt with explicit input placeholders and an expected result. Bind it to a shortcut only if the interface supports that; otherwise paste or load the saved prompt and verify that all placeholders were supplied.

name: Output style
summary: A set of instructions that fixes role, tone and format for every reply in a session.
needed_when: You always want shorter answers, always want explanations, or the agent is not a software engineer.
detail: Write the required tone, audience, and format in a reusable instruction section. Include it in the session brief or a supported style setting, then check a sample reply against it.

name: Role profile
summary: A role contract mapped to a runner configuration with verified capabilities and permissions.
needed_when: Several roles (coordinate, build, review) need different permissions and models.
detail: Define the role purpose, permitted actions, required capabilities, and result contract. Translate those requirements into the selected runner configuration and verify the effective tool set. Stop launch if a required permission boundary cannot be enforced.

name: "When to use which role" notes
summary: A short description that tells the coordinator which role to pick for which job.
needed_when: Several roles overlap and the coordinator needs an unambiguous route.
detail: Give each role a description naming the distinct task branch it handles and the result it returns. Test ambiguous tasks against the descriptions and merge roles that have no distinct responsibility.

name: Model, effort and thinking per role
summary: Choose and verify model settings per role when the runner supports separate configurations.
needed_when: Roles differ in cost or difficulty, such as heavy review versus light gathering.
detail: Use per-role model settings only when the runner supports them. Evaluate candidates on representative tasks, record the selected configuration, and verify what each worker actually uses. If overrides are unavailable, use the common model and report that constraint.

name: Shared working convention (mode)
summary: A shared convention document supplied to each role that needs it.
needed_when: Many roles need the same rhythm, such as loading principles, recording choices and reporting.
detail: Keep shared conventions in one short document and point each role brief to it. Verify each worker received it; do not assume a skill is automatically loaded once for every role.

name: Task authorization policy
summary: A task-specific authorization policy enforced before side effects.
needed_when: Some work is safe to run autonomously and some needs a person's approval.
detail: Record which actions may proceed, which require approval, and who can approve them. Enforce that policy at the executor boundary. If the runner cannot intercept the relevant actions, remove those capabilities or keep the work supervised.

name: Plan before editing
summary: A planning phase with read-only access followed by an explicitly authorized editing phase.
needed_when: The change is large or risky and the direction needs agreement first.
detail: Produce a plan using read-only tools or credentials, with proposed changes and validation. Wait at the agreed approval point before enabling writes. If there is no enforced read-only mode, provide snapshots for planning and apply approved edits in a separate run.

name: Role methodology document
summary: A document describing how one role works: sequence, checks and repeated errors.
needed_when: The role has a process longer than a profile page.
detail: Write one markdown file per role and link it from the router.

name: Lifecycle hook (foundation)
summary: A handler attached to a supported lifecycle event, with tested failure behavior.
needed_when: Something must happen every time without relying on the model to remember.
detail: Require documented lifecycle events with input, timeout, and failure semantics. Bind a small handler and test success, failure, and timeout. Without event interception, put the same check in the launcher or CI and state which actions it covers.

name: Pre-execution gate
summary: Validate an operation before execution through an enforceable interceptor.
needed_when: A "never" rule such as editing secrets, recursive deletes, or writing into forbidden directories.
detail: Require an executor or pre-execution interceptor that receives the intended operation and can deny it before side effects. Test both allowed and blocked fixtures, including interceptor failure. Without that boundary, remove the operation capability or isolate its credentials.

name: Post-edit hook (format, lint, quick test)
summary: A quick check after edits, automated when edit events are available.
needed_when: You want lint or type errors visible as code is produced.
detail: Run the relevant formatter or quick check through a supported edit event; capture failures without flooding context. If no edit event exists, run the check after each edit batch in the worker procedure.

name: Completion check
summary: Check completion evidence at the reporting boundary with an explicit warning or blocking policy.
needed_when: "Done" must be verifiable and a self-report is not enough.
detail: Run the completion check at the final reporting boundary. Choose warning or blocking behavior explicitly and cap retries. If the runner cannot intercept stopping, run the check in the launcher or CI and expose its result separately from the agent report.

name: Session-start context hook
summary: A bounded bootstrap step that validates prerequisites before the agent starts.
needed_when: You want a fixed bootstrap (load rules, check versions, check state) not left to reminders.
detail: Use a startup handler if supported; otherwise run a bootstrap command before launching the session. Verify required tools and state, stop on missing prerequisites, and pass only the relevant results into the brief.

name: Automatic permission-approval hook
summary: A deterministic policy answers supported permission requests within preauthorized bounds.
needed_when: Unattended runs still need conditional approval.
detail: Require an executor that can route permission requests through deterministic policy. Allow only operations with already established authorization, log the outcome, and deny or stop on unknown requests. If interception is unavailable, use narrowly scoped credentials and supervised execution.

name: Logging and notification hook
summary: Observe lifecycle events through available hooks or launcher instrumentation.
needed_when: You need an audit trail or a message when work finishes.
detail: Attach logging to documented lifecycle events or wrap worker launches. Write redacted records outside model context, test event delivery, and make log failures visible. Deliver notifications only through an authorized destination.

name: Allow, ask and deny permission rules
summary: An executor policy classifies operations and resolves overlapping rules explicitly.
needed_when: You need safe allowances (tests, lint) while still blocking sensitive files.
detail: Implement an explicit allow, ask, and deny policy in the executor and document overlap precedence. Test conflicting rules and alternate execution paths. If the runner cannot enforce a restriction, narrow credentials or remove the capability.

name: Permission modes
summary: A verified session permission configuration matched to the task.
needed_when: The right level differs by work: exploring, hand-editing, long runs, locked-down CI.
detail: Select a supported permission configuration for the role and verify its effective behavior with allowed and denied fixtures. If unattended execution cannot reject unsupported requests without prompting, keep the run supervised.

name: Model-based automatic approver
summary: An optional classifier assists operation review inside deterministic authorization limits.
needed_when: You want fewer prompts but still a block on irreversible actions.
detail: Use a classifier only when the executor exposes a review boundary. Keep deterministic restrictions outside the classifier, test false approvals, and route uncertain cases to a person or deny them. Without that boundary, omit classifier-based approval.

name: OS-level sandbox
summary: An operating-system boundary around shell commands for files and network.
needed_when: You want commands to run without asking each time while limiting harm.
detail: Require an OS or container sandbox that controls the relevant file and network operations. Configure minimum access and test blocked writes and connections from the actual worker process. If isolation is unavailable, use a controlled machine or stop tasks requiring that boundary.

name: File-scope fence
summary: An enforced filesystem boundary around the paths a role may access.
needed_when: A role may only touch one directory tree.
detail: Enforce filesystem access with a sandbox or equivalent executor boundary, including alternate shell paths and symlink resolution. Test permitted and forbidden reads and writes. If the boundary cannot be enforced, withhold the relevant credentials and tools or use an isolated environment.

name: Per-role tool fence
summary: A role-specific tool inventory backed by execution authorization.
needed_when: A review role should be read-only, or a build role must not touch the ticket tracker.
detail: Require a runner or gateway that can restrict executable tools per role. Verify both the exposed inventory and blocked execution. If separate inventories are unavailable, use a restricted gateway or separate credentials; a prompt alone is not a tool fence.

name: Ban on tiered sub-agent spawning
summary: A rule on who may open sub-agents, enforced by removing the tool rather than by instruction.
needed_when: You have supervisor, orchestrator and worker tiers and do not want workers to spawn more.
detail: If delegation is available, restrict child creation at the launcher or executor and enforce depth and concurrency limits. Test a disallowed child launch. If nested spawning cannot be controlled, run workers without delegation capability.

name: Outward writes need an explicit user statement
summary: Consequential external writes are tied to explicit user authorization and an enforceable scope.
needed_when: A mistaken write to an outside system is hard to undo.
detail: Record the authorized external action, scope, and user instruction before execution. Enforce that scope in a tool gateway or credential boundary. If enforcement is unavailable, require supervised execution for the consequential write.

name: Secrets and identity
summary: Credentials delivered to the executor without exposing them in instructions or results.
needed_when: An MCP server or CLI needs credentials and several people share configuration.
detail: Use the service authentication flow or a secret store that supplies credentials directly to the executor. Verify that prompts, command logs, and results redact secrets. If secure credential delivery is unavailable, stop the integration rather than embedding credentials in instructions.

name: Trust gate (folders, hooks, plugins)
summary: Review executable project configuration before granting it access to the working environment.
needed_when: You clone an unknown repository or accept plugins or hooks from others.
detail: Inspect repository-supplied hooks, plugins, and startup commands before enabling execution. Use a configuration-disabled launch or an isolated copy when supported. If configuration cannot be disabled, inspect the repository with ordinary read-only tools before launching the agent.

name: Organization policy (managed settings)
summary: Organization restrictions enforced through protected configuration or infrastructure.
needed_when: Many people or machines need the same limits on model, MCP, plugins and permissions.
detail: Require a protected configuration or enforcement layer for mandatory organization policy. Attempt an ordinary user override and verify rejection. If the runner has no protected layer, enforce restrictions through centrally controlled credentials or infrastructure.

name: "Warn first, strict later" check ladder
summary: Every new check only warns (exit 0); it becomes a hard block (exit 1) only under a strict flag with a recorded reason.
needed_when: A new check is not yet proven to have few false alarms and a hard block could stall the flow.
detail: Give each checker a strict flag; run it in warn mode for a while and promote it when false alarms are rare.

name: Shared versus private boundary check
summary: A scanner that confirms shareable documents and code do not leak project-specific terms.
needed_when: A common standard set is carried between projects.
detail: Keep a forbidden-strings file outside the shared folder and run the scanner in strict mode on every change.

name: Hard caps: turns, budget, time, agent count
summary: Enforced run limits on time, concurrency, and observable resource use.
needed_when: Unattended runs, multi-agent workflows and scheduled jobs.
detail: Record runtime, concurrency, and available usage budgets before launch. Enforce supported limits in the runner and unsupported limits in an external supervisor. If a required limit cannot be enforced, keep the run supervised or do not launch it.

name: Agent-to-agent trust is not user consent
summary: A rule that another agent's words do not replace a person's: no permission changes and no approvals on their behalf.
needed_when: Several agents message each other and you must stop permission escalation through messages.
detail: Treat agent messages as task data. Check requested permission changes against the original user authorization at the executor boundary, and reject relayed approvals that lack a verifiable authorized origin.

name: Protected acceptance criteria
summary: Stable acceptance criteria with evidence-backed status and controlled amendments.
needed_when: The work spans many sessions and the agent tends to declare done early or delete hard criteria.
detail: Seed criteria with evidence requirements and protect their text from worker edits. Record a passing result only with its check evidence; invalidate stale passes after relevant changes. Amend criteria through a separate reviewed change.

name: Progress log across sessions
summary: A file recording what was done, what is in progress and the next step, read first by the next session.
needed_when: Every session starts with empty context.
detail: Append one dated line per finished step with its evidence; the next session reads the last lines first.

name: Two phases: initialize, then work incrementally
summary: The first session builds the environment, spec and criteria list; later sessions advance one item at a time.
needed_when: The project is too large for one context window.
detail: Write two prompts, an initializer and a worker, and have the worker stop after one verified item.

name: Read before work, verify before continuing
summary: At the start of each session the agent must read the spec, list, log and git history and run regression tests before new work.
needed_when: The previous session may have left a defect.
detail: Make "get your bearings" and "run the verification test" the first two steps of the worker prompt.

name: Work lifecycle state machine
summary: The states and transitions of a work item: received, in which phase, awaiting review, done, sent back.
needed_when: Many tickets run in parallel across phases and you need to know where each stands.
detail: Describe the states in one document; add code only if you need transitions enforced.

name: Task list with dependencies and claiming
summary: An internal queue: create tasks, declare dependencies, agents claim ready tasks.
needed_when: Several parallel workers handle independent pieces.
detail: Use a task store with atomic claims, dependency checks, and recovery of abandoned claims. If the available task list lacks those guarantees, let one coordinator assign tasks serially and record ownership before dispatch.

name: Current-state file
summary: A single "current truth" file for a task, edited in place rather than stacking summaries.
needed_when: Context changes, agents change, or the conversation is compacted.
detail: Keep one file per task, overwrite stale facts, and link it from the brief.

name: Choice log and review states
summary: A record of consequential choices and their review status.
needed_when: An agent must choose for a person who reviews later and a "why" trail is needed.
detail: Keep an append-only choice record with question, options, selected action, reason, approver, and status. Add commands only when transitions need enforcement; stop before hard-to-reverse actions whose required approval is absent.

name: Human approval gate (stop point)
summary: A mandatory point where a person looks and approves before work continues.
needed_when: A step is hard to reverse, or a phase changes.
detail: Name the gates in the workflow document and make the agent stop and ask there.

name: Structured output and result template
summary: Results checked against a schema or template before downstream use.
needed_when: A result feeds an automatic step or a hand-off between agents.
detail: Define the result schema or template and validate the produced artifact before downstream use. Enable schema-constrained generation only where supported. Handle refusal, incomplete output, and validation failure as explicit outcomes rather than valid data.

name: Recovery point
summary: A verified snapshot with explicit restoration scope.
needed_when: The agent damages several files.
detail: Create a verified snapshot before risky changes and record exactly which state it covers. Test restoration on a disposable fixture; use version control or backups when runtime checkpoints are absent. External writes require their own compensation plan.

name: Sessions: name, resume, fork
summary: Continue or branch work through supported session persistence or a durable handoff.
needed_when: Work spans days, or you want to try another approach from the same point.
detail: When session persistence is available, record its identifier and verify the resumed objective and live state. Branch only if the runner supports independent histories. Otherwise start a new session from a durable handoff and reconcile current files before work.

name: Hand-off
summary: Moving the task and the context it needs to another agent or session.
needed_when: You change agent, change platform, or run out of context.
detail: Use a hand-off skill that writes goal, state, choices made and next step into one document.

name: Run trace (transcript and logs)
summary: A redacted run record with known coverage for later investigation.
needed_when: Investigating an error or checking what was really done.
detail: Find the runner log and export interfaces, then verify they capture a sample operation and result. If exports are absent, have the launcher record redacted inputs, outputs, exit status, and run identity. State coverage gaps.

name: Retention and cleanup
summary: Rules for how long to keep things and what is cleaned automatically.
needed_when: Disk grows from scratch notes, snapshots and old worktrees.
detail: List artifacts, owners, and retention periods. Preview cleanup targets and exclude active runs or unmerged work before deletion. Use runtime retention controls only where their scope is documented; handle other files with an explicit cleanup command.

name: Registry of running agents
summary: A record of which agents are running, whose, who the parent is, and the configuration fingerprint at spawn.
needed_when: Many agents run and you must know who the parent is to return results and which are stale.
detail: Use an agent-list API only if it exposes the needed identity and lifecycle fields. Otherwise maintain a registry through the launcher, reconcile it against live processes, and mark stale entries rather than treating them as running.

name: External systems through MCP
summary: Connect external tools and data through the Model Context Protocol when both endpoints support it.
needed_when: You keep copying data from a browser tab the agent cannot see.
detail: Require compatible MCP client and server implementations with a negotiated protocol revision and supported transport. Test tool listing and a read-only call before writes. If the runner lacks MCP, use a service API, CLI, or explicit export; schema loading strategy is a client choice.

name: CLI or script the agent calls
summary: A command-line program in the repository that the agent runs through its shell tool.
needed_when: The outside system already has a CLI, or you need a repeatable, checkable action with short output.
detail: Prefer a CLI when one exists and keep MCP for systems without one; make output short and errors name the next step.

name: Skill with scripts
summary: A skill that bundles scripts or references its SKILL.md calls.
needed_when: An operation needs reliable code instead of the model rewriting it each time.
detail: For an Agent Skills-compatible loader, put reusable code in the skill scripts directory and reference it relative to the skill root. Verify path resolution and required dependencies. Without skill execution support, call the script explicitly from the task procedure.

name: Plugin (distribution package)
summary: A versioned bundle of reusable components with an explicit installation contract.
needed_when: A second repository needs the same setup.
detail: If the runner supports plugin packages, follow its manifest and installation contract and test installation and removal in a disposable profile. Otherwise distribute a versioned bundle with an explicit setup script and declared dependencies.

name: Package index and versions
summary: A reviewed index of reusable packages and pinned versions.
needed_when: You want to publish, update or restrict plugin sources.
detail: Record package origin, immutable version, integrity evidence, and update policy. Use a supported package index if available; otherwise maintain a reviewed manifest and install from pinned sources. Verify that an upgrade can be rolled back.

name: Interface extension
summary: Optional interface extensions built against a documented extension API.
needed_when: You want to change the interface or behavior at the product layer, beyond configuration.
detail: Require a documented interface-extension API and supported lifecycle. Keep the extension optional, declare compatibility, and test install, disable, and cleanup in a disposable profile. If no API exists, use an external companion view instead of patching private interfaces.

name: Programming SDK
summary: Embed agent runs through a supported SDK or programmable entry point.
needed_when: You turn webhooks or issues into tasks, run many agents in parallel, or build a dashboard.
detail: Require a supported programmable agent entry point. Wrap startup, cancellation, result parsing, and errors in an adapter; enforce limits in the adapter or supervisor and test a failed run. If no SDK exists, use a documented noninteractive CLI; otherwise keep execution manual.

name: Headless run (exec)
summary: A bounded noninteractive run with observable status and validated output.
needed_when: You embed the agent in a pipeline, a schedule or a hook.
detail: Require a noninteractive entry point with observable completion and cancellation. Supply a bounded brief, restrict credentials, capture status and output, and validate the result. If the interface requires interaction or cannot signal failure, stop pipeline integration.

name: Browser and computer control
summary: The agent opens pages, clicks, types and takes screenshots to check an interface.
needed_when: UI or web flows that unit tests cannot see.
detail: Require a browser or desktop automation interface with appropriate permissions. Drive a representative flow and capture the resulting state. If automation is unavailable, use a manual verification checklist and label the evidence as manual.

name: Background progress monitor
summary: Observe background progress through event streaming or bounded polling.
needed_when: You wait on a build, a log or a push status and do not want to spend turns.
detail: Use event streaming or process output subscriptions when available, with a terminal event and cancellation path. Otherwise poll a status endpoint at bounded intervals and stop at completion or timeout. Keep full logs outside the conversation.

name: Supervised long-running scripts and services
summary: Long-running commands with explicit readiness, logging, and cleanup.
needed_when: The agent must start a dev server, a database or long tests in the same workspace.
detail: Use a process supervisor that records process identity, readiness, logs, ports, and shutdown behavior. Start from explicit commands and verify readiness before dependent work. If no supervisor exists, use an external process manager or keep the service in a managed foreground session.

name: Role launcher
summary: A thin adapter from role requirements to a verified runner invocation.
needed_when: Many roles need identical configuration on every spawn and you do not want to rely on people remembering flags.
detail: Keep the launcher as the only translation from role requirements to runner arguments. Validate required capabilities before launch, offer a print-only resolved configuration, and test the emitted invocation against the installed runner.

name: Pin external tool versions
summary: Fixing the version of MCP servers, libraries and third-party skills.
needed_when: You want to avoid silent behavior change when an outside party ships a new release.
detail: Record exact versions in the config or lock file and re-check them when you upgrade.

name: Tool search on demand
summary: Retrieve tool schemas on demand when supported; otherwise reduce the configured tool inventory.
needed_when: Many MCP servers or tools bloat the context.
detail: Use deferred schema retrieval only when the client exposes that capability and preserves correct discovery. Test finding and invoking a rarely used tool. Otherwise configure a smaller tool set per task and remove unused integrations.

name: Tool errors always name the next step
summary: Every error or limit message from a tool has a "fix:" line saying what to do next.
needed_when: The agent hits an error and either stops silently or guesses.
detail: Add a fix line to each error path in your scripts and test that it appears.

name: Sub-agent (isolated worker, returns a summary)
summary: A worker with bounded task context and an explicit result contract.
needed_when: A side task floods the conversation with output you will not reference again.
detail: Require isolated worker contexts and a result-return channel. Supply a focused brief, permissions, and evidence contract; verify what context the worker inherits. If delegation is unavailable, run the side task in a separate session and import its report.

name: Parallel sessions
summary: Several independent sessions at once, coordinated by hand or by an agent.
needed_when: There are several independent tasks that should not run in sequence.
detail: Give each session its own worktree and brief; collect results from files rather than from chat.

name: Agent team with task list and mailbox
summary: Workers coordinate through a task store and messaging interface when both are available.
needed_when: The work needs teammates who discuss and challenge each other, not sequential steps.
detail: Require task ownership, worker messaging, and lifecycle reporting before using a team. Assign nonoverlapping scope and start with the smallest useful team. If those capabilities are missing, use independent sessions with a single coordinator and explicit handoffs.

name: Dynamic workflow (orchestration script)
summary: A bounded orchestration script dispatches tasks and reconciles their results.
needed_when: The work exceeds a few sub-agents or needs cross-checked results, such as a repository-wide audit.
detail: Build a reviewed script against an available worker API or noninteractive CLI. Bound concurrency and retries, persist task identities, and aggregate failures as well as successes. If no programmable launcher exists, split the audit into manually dispatched batches.

name: Messaging between sessions and agents
summary: Task-scoped messages between sessions with explicit delivery and processing state.
needed_when: One session breaks something another depends on, or one session settles a question another is blocked on.
detail: Use authenticated messaging with run and task identities, delivery acknowledgment, and documented queue behavior. If messaging is unavailable, write a durable handoff record for the coordinator to deliver. Never assume delivery means the recipient has acted.

name: Parent-child relay
summary: A process that follows child agents and pushes their final report to the parent, with logging and a "delivered" state.
needed_when: The parent does not want to poll and the child must report automatically when done.
detail: Observe child completion through a supported event or process supervisor, persist the final report, and deliver it with an idempotent message ID. Mark delivered only after acknowledgment. If push is unavailable, have the parent read the durable completion record.

name: Coordination tiers and width limits
summary: A tree of roles (supervisor, orchestrator, worker): who may open whom and how many.
needed_when: Many tickets and phases need one point of contact with the user.
detail: Document the tiers and enforce the limits in the launcher rather than in prose.

name: Maintenance inbox for the harness keeper
summary: A fixed folder where any role leaves "work only the maintainer can do"; items move to a read folder once handled.
needed_when: An agent finds a harness defect but is not allowed to fix it itself.
detail: Define the folder and a one-file-per-item format; the maintainer clears it on a schedule.

name: Multi-provider coordination
summary: Coordinate provider-specific adapters behind a shared task and result contract.
needed_when: You want cross-opinions or each provider's strengths.
detail: Define a provider-independent task and result contract, then map each provider through a tested adapter. Verify required permissions and cancellation for each adapter. If a provider lacks a required capability, keep that task on a compatible runner.

name: Advisor, second opinion, committee
summary: An independent review of a difficult choice using a compact evidence brief.
needed_when: You are about to commit to a direction, are stuck on a repeating failure, or about to declare done.
detail: Send an independent reviewer a compact question, evidence, and constraints; request a recommendation with unresolved gaps. If a separate agent is unavailable, use a human reviewer or an explicitly separate review session.

name: Multi-machine coordination
summary: Coordinate work across machines with explicit identities, status, and trust boundaries.
needed_when: A powerful remote machine, or a shared team setup.
detail: Require authenticated launch and status channels to each machine, a machine/run registry, and scoped credentials. Record execution location and test disconnect recovery. If a central hub is absent, use explicit per-machine launch adapters and a shared status record.

name: Runnable check (tests, typecheck, CI)
summary: Evidence that checks the result against its acceptance criteria.
needed_when: A result must be distinguished from an unsupported completion claim.
detail: Name an appropriate runnable check when available and retain its output. For outcomes that need human judgment, state the review criterion and reviewer. If verification cannot be performed, report the result as unverified instead of inventing a passing check.

name: Eval for harness artifacts
summary: A set of graded test cases for skills, plugins, prompts and roles, rerun when the harness or the model changes.
needed_when: You change a skill, instruction or role profile and cannot tell if quality dropped.
detail: Keep cases with inputs, expected behavior, and a grader. Run them through a supported evaluation interface or a small runner adapter, preserve outcomes, and compare changed and baseline versions under the same conditions.

name: Automatic and local code review
summary: An agent reads a diff or pull request and verifies findings before reporting.
needed_when: Before merge, to catch logic, security and edge-case defects.
detail: Give the reviewer the diff, relevant requirements, and check results. Require each reported defect to identify a concrete failing path and supporting evidence. Use a review integration if available; otherwise run a separate review session.

name: Independent reviewer; builder does not self-grade
summary: Changes to behavior-controlling files must be graded by another agent or person.
needed_when: You edit instruction files, profiles, skills or the launcher.
detail: Give a separate agent or person the change, requirements, and evidence using read-only access. Record findings and resolution. If no independent reviewer is available, expose that gap rather than presenting self-review as independent.

name: Security scan while writing code
summary: The agent reviews its own change for vulnerabilities and fixes them in the same session.
needed_when: You want less security-review load later.
detail: Add a change-specific security review step covering affected trust boundaries and data flows. Use available scanners for concrete checks and verify reported findings before applying fixes; record any untested boundary.

name: Stale-agent detection by configuration fingerprint
summary: At spawn, store a hash of prompt, settings, MCP, skills and launcher flags; later compare with the current hash to learn that a running agent uses outdated configuration.
needed_when: You edit a profile or skill mid-run and old agents keep running the old version.
detail: Hash the inputs at spawn into the registry and report a mismatch in the status view.

name: Effective configuration and dry run
summary: A command that prints the configuration that would really be used (which source wins, which flags) without running.
needed_when: You suspect configuration did not apply, or want to check before spawning.
detail: Expose a print-only launcher command that resolves configuration sources and required capabilities. Use runner inspection APIs where available and compare observed behavior with the resolved settings. Label settings whose effective value cannot be inspected.

name: Quality audit of instructions and skills
summary: A tool that inspects instructions and skills for length, contradiction and vague descriptions.
needed_when: Instructions grow, or skill descriptions overlap.
detail: Review trigger descriptions, duplicated rules, contradictory guidance, and steps without completion criteria. Use simple scripts for measurable properties and a reader for meaning; validate a representative task after editing.

name: Cost and usage measurement
summary: Tokens and money per session, role and day.
needed_when: You run many agents and need caps and alerts.
detail: Read documented usage records when available and aggregate by run and role. Keep estimated cost separate from billed usage, enforce observable limits in the supervisor, and disclose missing metrics instead of treating them as zero.

name: Telemetry (OpenTelemetry)
summary: Export supported run signals through OpenTelemetry or retain structured logs when export is unavailable.
needed_when: Production or team use where you must know what agents do.
detail: Require an OpenTelemetry exporter or instrument the launcher with OpenTelemetry libraries. Correlate traces with run identity, redact sensitive content, and verify receipt at a collector. Without telemetry support, retain structured local logs.

name: Tests for the harness itself
summary: Automated tests for the launcher, checkers and tools of the harness.
needed_when: The harness has code you wrote.
detail: Write small tests that run each checker on good and bad samples and assert the exit code and message.

name: Turn an incident into a test case
summary: Each incident produces an eval or test so it is caught next time.
needed_when: A defect repeats or slipped through review.
detail: Add a line to the incident log and a matching case in the check set before closing the incident.

name: Regression on model or system-prompt change
summary: Rerun checks when a new model ships or the harness changes, and remove obsolete components.
needed_when: You upgrade the model or notice quality shift.
detail: Keep a fixed check set and rerun it on every model or prompt change; record the scores.

name: Re-read the live source before writing (unattended jobs)
summary: Before recording state, read the source again; a failed source is reported as "unreadable", not "nothing new".
needed_when: Scheduled jobs that pull outside data.
detail: Make the job distinguish a read error from an empty result and write the error to the log.

name: Evidence rule (stated, inferred, open)
summary: A reporting rule that separates what the source says, what is inferred and what is unchecked; check the real artifact at the right revision.
needed_when: An agent reports to another agent or to a person who decides.
detail: Require every claim to carry one of the three labels and a source or command output.

name: Commit and pull-request gate
summary: A command that checks commit trailers and stray lines before merge.
needed_when: The target project has commit or pull-request conventions.
detail: Run the checker in warn mode first and promote to strict once false alarms are rare.

name: Verify by driving the real app
summary: A skill that sets up how to run the app like a user and proves behavior.
needed_when: The project has no scripted way to verify UI, CLI or service behavior.
detail: Write a representative user flow, expected observable result, and cleanup steps. Run it through an available UI, CLI, or service test interface; if automation is unavailable, use a manual check and record that limitation.

name: Retrospective (after-action review)
summary: A look back at a session or task that draws lessons and proposes changes to skills, instructions or profiles.
needed_when: The same kind of error repeats, or at the end of a batch of work.
detail: Use a retro skill that proposes edits for a person to accept; do not let it rewrite instructions silently.

name: "Wrong twice, write it down" rule
summary: When an agent errs the same way twice or review repeats a comment, edit the instruction or skill instead of correcting in chat.
needed_when: A mistake or review finding repeats despite a prior correction.
detail: When the same error recurs, identify its cause and change the relevant guard, test, or instruction. Keep the lesson at one authoritative location and verify it against a regression case.

name: Encode a lesson in structure, not more text
summary: A priority order for preventing repeat errors: architecture, types, a lint whose message names the fix, a test, and documentation last.
needed_when: You wrote the same reminder a second time.
detail: Try the earliest option in the order that can enforce the rule; write the doc line only if none can.

name: Failure-class catalog
summary: A table classifying the errors seen (design, build, operation, verification) to show distribution and gaps.
needed_when: You want to know where the harness breaks most.
detail: Keep one table with a row per class and a count; update it from each incident. A workable starting set: A. Wrong text (contradictions, stale wording left after a rule change); B. Inefficient tools (wasted context, duplicate messages, state files never cleaned up); C. Stale running agents (prompt, config or tool changed but a live agent did not reload); D. Not reviewable later (no history, drifting commit codes); E. Outside A-D (state or gate models that drift from the user's intent, role and channel fences, skipped procedures, harness versus product boundary). Give each class one general prevention and attach real examples in the project's own document.

name: Prune components when a new model ships
summary: Periodically remove each harness component and re-measure whether it is still needed.
needed_when: You upgrade the model, or the harness has grown heavy.
detail: Remove one component at a time, rerun the check set, and keep the removal if scores hold.

name: Measured improvement (hill-climbing)
summary: Editing prompts or skills in a loop with scores, separate train and test sets, and a noise measurement first.
needed_when: You have an eval set and want a controlled score increase.
detail: Measure run-to-run noise before changing anything and accept a change only when it beats the noise on held-out cases.

name: Maintenance loop by the harness keeper
summary: A procedure for editing the harness: log before coding, reread with a command, measure before fixing, fix the tool instead of adding a second check.
needed_when: The harness has a dedicated keeper.
detail: Write the loop as a short checklist in the maintainer's document.

name: In-session loop (recurring prompt)
summary: A bounded periodic check during an active session.
needed_when: Watching a pull request, build or deploy while you work.
detail: Require a timer that can invoke a check while the session is active. Set an interval, stop condition, and run cap; prevent overlapping invocations. If the runner has no timer, use an external monitor and bring its final result into the session.

name: Durable schedule
summary: A recurring job executed by a persistent scheduler independent of an interactive session.
needed_when: A weekly retro, a morning triage or branch cleanup.
detail: Use a scheduler independent of the interactive session, with a durable job definition, timezone, overlap policy, and failure reporting. Verify a run after the client disconnects and test missed-run behavior. If no persistent runner is available, keep the task manual.

name: CI/CD integration
summary: Run a bounded agent job from a pipeline event or schedule.
needed_when: You want automatic pull-request review or pull requests generated from issues.
detail: Require a CI runner and a supported noninteractive agent entry point. Restrict event types, job permissions, and secrets; enforce timeout and retain results. Keep deterministic required checks separate from model review.

name: Unattended run: permissions and caps
summary: Configuration so a scheduled job does not hang on a permission dialog or burn without limit.
needed_when: Any background job (J01 to J04).
detail: Verify that unauthorized operations fail without an interactive prompt. Use minimum credentials, an external timeout, and available usage limits; test cancellation and failure reporting. If prompts cannot be eliminated safely, keep the job supervised.

name: Bookmark and source state for scheduled jobs
summary: The job remembers how far it read from each source rather than "the last 24 hours".
needed_when: Pulling issues or documents on a schedule.
detail: Store a per-source marker; on a read error keep the old marker and report "unreadable".

name: Notifications
summary: Telling a person when attention is needed or work is done.
needed_when: Long background work while the person is away.
detail: Choose an authorized notification destination and define the events that merit interruption. Include run identity, result, and action needed; test delivery and deduplicate retries. If push delivery is unavailable, leave a durable status record for scheduled review.

name: Live monitoring and agent lifetime
summary: Alerts when an agent runs too long or hangs.
needed_when: Many background agents.
detail: Record progress timestamps and enforce a runtime deadline through a supervisor. Detect missing heartbeats, capture diagnostics, and restart only operations with a tested recovery path; otherwise alert and preserve state.

name: Recovery after a crash or restart
summary: What happens to background work when a process dies or the machine shuts down.
needed_when: Long-running jobs.
detail: Persist checkpoints and operation identities after verified steps. On restart, reconcile external state before repeating side effects; test crash recovery and the selected scheduler missed-run policy. Leave ambiguous operations unresolved for review.

name: Remote and cloud execution
summary: Execute work on a persistent remote runner with verified lifecycle behavior.
needed_when: Long work and a desk machine that cannot stay open.
detail: Require a remote runner that remains active independently of the local client. Verify source checkout, credential scope, result retrieval, and cancellation, then test disconnect behavior. If unavailable, use a persistent local supervisor or postpone the long run.

name: Staged release of harness changes
summary: Putting a harness change into use through a channel with rollback.
needed_when: The harness has many users or projects.
detail: Version the harness, roll out to one representative project, run its checks, and compare outcomes before broadening. Retain the prior version and a tested rollback procedure; use release channels only if the distribution system provides them.

name: Upgrade procedure (model, CLI, pinned skills)
summary: A check procedure when the model or CLI version changes.
needed_when: The model, runner, or pinned dependency version changes.
detail: After upgrading, verify resolved configuration, required tool capabilities, and representative task checks. Compare results with the prior version and retain a rollback path.

name: Layered configuration scopes
summary: Configuration scopes with verified precedence and explicit override boundaries.
needed_when: Individuals want overrides that stay out of the repository, or an organization wants enforcement.
detail: List the configuration scopes actually supported by the runner and test their precedence. Keep local overrides out of version control; place mandatory restrictions in a protected enforcement layer. If layering is absent, generate one resolved configuration.

name: Share through git
summary: Commit configuration, skills, hooks and agents so the whole team gets the same version.
needed_when: The team has more than one person.
detail: Commit reusable configuration and procedures with pinned dependencies. Keep secrets and personal overrides in ignored or external storage; verify setup from a clean checkout.

name: Common standard and project-specific part
summary: Separating a standard that can move to other projects from the project's own part.
needed_when: Several projects share a harness.
detail: Keep the shared part in its own folder with a boundary check, and let each project add a thin private layer.

name: Audit log
summary: A trace sufficient to answer "which agent did what, under which choice".
needed_when: Compliance, incidents, or disputes over a choice.
detail: Log each tool call with its allow, ask or deny result, an identity and a request id, kept apart from content.

name: Share outputs and onboarding guides
summary: Export results as a viewable page, send files, create a guide for teammates.
needed_when: The result is clearer visually than as text, or a new teammate joins.
detail: Export the result in a format the recipient can open, include an entry point and prerequisites, and verify the rendered artifact. Use an authorized sharing destination; if sharing tools are absent, provide the local artifact for the user to distribute.

name: File ownership per agent
summary: Each agent owns its own set of files so no two edit the same file.
needed_when: Several parallel workers share one repository.
detail: Assign file sets in the brief and break work along those lines.

name: Roles and membership permissions
summary: Membership permissions enforced by the service or execution infrastructure.
needed_when: Many people and permissions must be separated, such as cloud sessions.
detail: Map people or service identities to required operations and enforce access in the service or infrastructure. Test a permitted and denied identity. If the product lacks membership controls, separate credentials or environments; documentation alone does not enforce access.

name: Git worktree per task
summary: A separate directory and branch for each session or agent so they do not trample each other.
needed_when: Several tasks in parallel on one repository.
detail: In a Git repository, create a linked worktree on a separate branch for each concurrent editing task. Check for uncommitted or unmerged work before removal. Worktrees separate working files, while shared Git metadata and external resources still need coordination.

name: Environment lifecycle: setup, teardown, ignored files to copy
summary: Idempotent setup and cleanup of a task environment with explicit local inputs.
needed_when: A new worktree lacks dependencies and local configuration.
detail: Write idempotent setup and cleanup commands and an explicit allowlist of local configuration to supply. Invoke them from workspace lifecycle events if supported, otherwise from the task launcher. Verify a clean setup and preserve secrets outside tracked files.

name: Per-task resources (database, port)
summary: Each ticket gets its own database or port, with locks on shared ones to prevent overlap.
needed_when: Tests use a real database and several agents run in parallel.
detail: Derive the database name and port from the ticket id and refuse to start if it is taken.

name: Source data mirror
summary: Pull outside data into a local copy used as a stable read source instead of reading live.
needed_when: The source is in a document store and runs must be repeatable.
detail: Write a sync script that pulls into a mirror folder and stamps the date of the copy.

name: Vendoring and dependency copies
summary: Keeping a copy of outside code or skills inside the repository so runs repeat.
needed_when: You do not want to depend on network or outside versions; it costs space and can drift.
detail: Vendor only what you must, record the upstream version, and check for drift on a schedule.

name: Machine isolation (container, VM)
summary: Run risky or untrusted work inside a verified disposable environment.
needed_when: Task execution requires isolation from the normal working machine.
detail: Require a container or VM with controlled mounts, credentials, and network access. Test the boundaries from inside the worker and destroy the environment after collecting results. If adequate isolation is unavailable, retain restrictive execution permissions.

name: Review shared-data links before merging worktrees
summary: Prevent accidental tracking of links to local shared data during worktree integration.
needed_when: A worktree needs data from ignored folders such as vendor or data.
detail: Keep shared ignored data outside tracked worktree changes and reference it through configuration. Before merging, inspect changed paths and symlink entries with git diff --summary against the merge base; investigate unexpected mode 120000 entries and verify the target tree.

name: Multi-session overview and progress
summary: An overview of run state, freshness, and pending user action.
needed_when: Many background sessions.
detail: Build a view from the verified run registry and observed lifecycle events, showing last update, pending input, completion, and failure. Use a native view if it exposes those fields; otherwise render a table from the registry and mark stale status explicitly.

name: Result template and brief template
summary: Fixed forms for hand-off reports and for delegated tasks.
needed_when: Many agents return results to a parent and the parent needs to read and compare quickly.
detail: Keep two small template files and reference them from the role profiles.

name: Report with sources and certainty labels
summary: A research report format: source (id, URL, date read), verbatim quote, and a split of "stated / inferred / open".
needed_when: A report is the basis for a choice.
detail: Define the table columns once and require them in every research hand-off.

name: Presentation conventions (language, paths)
summary: Fixed rules for language, absolute paths and backtick use.
needed_when: Many agents write for the same reader.
detail: Write the rules in the root instructions or an output style.

name: Design documents, ADRs and specs
summary: Written records of architectural choices and specifications.
needed_when: A choice is hard to reverse and the reason must be kept.
detail: Use one short file per choice with question, options, reason and consequence.

name: Commit and pull-request text
summary: A fixed form for commit messages (trailers) and pull-request bodies.
needed_when: The target project's conventions require it.
detail: Use a PR-writing skill and a commit template; add a checker if the convention is strict.

name: Conventions for writing agent documents (one idea one place, length)
summary: General rules for writing for agents: short, each idea once, pointers instead of copies, neutral examples.
needed_when: Documents grow and contradict each other.
detail: Keep files short, link instead of copy, and give each rule one home.

name: Harness review checklist
summary: A fixed six-point list that an independent reviewer applies to every change touching files that steer agent behavior.
needed_when: A change touches agent-steering files (root instructions, role profiles, skill bodies, launcher, checkers) and the author must not grade it alone.
detail: Run it in a separate reviewer role with a clean context that receives the diff since the previous review plus the choices approved in that range; score all six points even when one has no finding. 1) When a concept is renamed, changed or dropped, search the whole repo for the old wording and contradicting sentences. 2) One source of truth: pointers, not a second copy of a rule. 3) Every step has a completion condition of the right kind (a checkable one for fragile or side-effecting steps, goal and constraints for judgment steps); text says what to do; each prohibition carries its reason and the replacement action. 4) Text matches code: commands, flags, paths and `fix:` messages exist and are still right (run with `--help` or try them, do not only read). 5) Tests check behavior (exit code, output, files produced), not document wording. 6) Approved choices show in both text and code; name which components need a fresh agent and which live agents will now be stale. The report does not block; one pass per work item. Where the reviewer role lives, where its report is written and how it is opened are project-specific.
